articles.title: State Hackers Weaponize Commercial AI Tools to Breach Global Infrastructure
articles.content: Agentic offensive framework automates familiar attack techniques, with weak defenses potentially breached in minutes Connor Jones Connor Jones Cybersecurity reporter Published thu 26 Nov 2026 // 19:04 UTC Make us preferred on Google Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories 7 hours ago Microsoft hotpatches hotpatch that could crash Windows Server 2025 12 hours ago Microsoft's NTLM security changes trip up third-party logins 1 day ago Microsoft fixes Office dialog that had nothing to say and wouldn't go away 1 day ago Microsoft 365 Backup stretches recovery window to ten years 1 day ago Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the  ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. "Threat actors define scope and targets for ARTEX, which then uses AI agents to set verifiable goals, define tactical steps for each stage of the operation, use tools to attack targets, create graphs to track discovered systems and results of actions, and report back to the threat actor." Notably, ARTEX does not offer any new attack techniques. All of the tool's capabilities were previously known to the cybersecurity world, but its value lies in the automation capabilities it offers users, chaining attacks at machine speed. In the UK NCSC's warning about AOFs this week, it said the key strengths of this technology are its speed, its thoroughness in probing target systems for weaknesses, how it learns from failures instantly, and that it is inexpensive to run at scale. AOFs' speed comes at a cost, however. These tools are noisy, the NCSC said, making them easier to detect in network logs and by defensive solutions. Some examples of the attacks in which the tool has been implicated include Storm-0940's hit on ConnectWise, which enabled attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, various financial institutions in South Korea and India , UK registrar 123 Reg , and the European Commission . ® microsoft china artex north korea security Make us preferred on Google

articles.title: DeepMind Grants Autonomous Agents Direct Control Over Training Clusters
articles.content: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant Google Deepmind lets AI agents run experiments on their own for the next Gemini model. On the company's podcast, VP of Research Koray Kavukcuoglu, who leads Gemini development, frames this as part of a strategic shift at the lab. Rather than running separate teams for specialized projects like AlphaFold and nuclear fusion, Deepmind now relies on a single general-purpose algorithm for both science and products, he says. Each Gemini generation, he adds, is a hand-built one-off rather than a fixed architecture, while parallel teams work on its successors. According to Kavukcuoglu, AI agents control part of the compute themselves to run experiments, though the lab is still far from full recursive self-improvement. As a safety measure, Deepmind doesn't reward the agents' internal thought streams ("Chain of Thought") during training, he says, so their intentions stay unfiltered and reviewable in natural language before they act. Kavukcuoglu also points to limits. Today's AI can depict physical processes such as fluid flows and collisions with visual accuracy, he says, but doesn't understand them precisely. No test can show when models will close those gaps and reach artificial general intelligence (AGI), he argues, because no benchmark captures the core of intelligence. In his view, AGI won't begin until useful everyday products earn enough trust for people to hand decisions over to them, the way they would when working with other people. articles.title: Reddit Aggressively Monetizes User Discussion Archives for Model Training Sets
articles.content: Reddit boasts engagement metrics that would be the envy of many other online platforms: Over 80% of its monetization comes from loyal, logged-in users, who spend eight times as much time on the site in their fifth year as they did in their first. And yet, Reddit’s share price is down 62% for the year to date, as the platform grapples with an internet increasingly shaped by AI. In its Q3 earnings call in October, Reddit’s CEO, Steve Huffman, said Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode were leading to a decline in search referrals to the site, the lifeblood of many social and media-adjacent businesses. The market did not like the implications, and the share price dropped from just shy of $130 apiece to a little under $91 overnight. Recommended Video Chief Operating Officer Jen Wong told Fortune in an exclusive interview that some factors were lost in translation. The shifting relationship between Reddit and search engines “requires a different kind of partnership,” she said, rather than any separation. If anything, Wong believes Reddit is well-positioned to navigate the new era of online information gathering. In their first year on Reddit, users tend to spend five minutes a day on the app or website. By their fifth year, that figure rises to 40 minutes, Wong tells Fortune . The number of “communities” (topic-focused discussion groups) that users are in jumps from 10 in the first year to more than 100 by their fifth. “Reddit is really interesting because we have users who have over a decade of karma,” Wong said. “Reddit typically gets you as a young adult, and then you season over time in this incredible way. If you look at the chart, it’s very consistent.” Wong sees users’ changing life stages reflected in the communities they join: “[They’ve] gone through life with Reddit. You started as a student, you got your first rental place, you got married, you had kids, and we see kind of your life’s journey. “You just never age out of Reddit because all of those life stages are available to you on Reddit, and you’re always going through something that you have to traverse.” Navigating different life stages appears to be a key differentiator of the Reddit platform. In 2024, an article published in “Higher Education Research and Development” found that one in three students use Reddit for study help, ahead of TikTok at 14.9% and Instagram at 12.7%. YouTube leads the pack, with more than 90% of the 1,000 students surveyed using it for educational purposes. The site’s leadership wants to expand on that function. In early November, Reddit launched Reddit Reviews, organizing product feedback across multiple communities to provide overall ratings. “Logged-in users season very, very well, which is another motivation for us to say we want more logged-in users, because we want the opportunity to teach you about all these other aspects of Reddit,” Wong adds, “Not just the information and retrieval part of Reddit, but the part of Reddit that is around the connection, the communities, and the conversation.” Every media platform needs to maintain or grow its audience. But Reddit has a unique problem: It has more than 100,000 “communities,” according to various reports, all of which have volunteer moderators. These moderators are unpaid and are not Reddit employees, instead choosing to spend their free time building their communities and ensuring the content is fit for its purpose. But with ever-evolving channels and new voices within them, demand for experienced moderators is high—in fact, Reddit even has a dedicated page where communities can recruit volunteer moderators. In the recruitment group, individuals are either looking for or offering moderation skills for hours a day, on a daily basis. Posts include requests for moderators in specific time zones, often for about 3 hours a day. But Wong says even if Reddit wanted to bring its moderators in-house and pay them, they probably wouldn’t take it. While moderators are interested in earning, she said, they didn’t want strings attached: “They really like their independence from us, to be able to say, ‘This is our community, we set the rules, and this is how we want to operate.’ “Our relationship with moderators, I think, has greatly improved. I’ve been with Reddit eight, almost nine years, and where at the beginning we were not investing as much as we could in creating moderator tools and making their lives better in terms of reducing some of the repetitive work, over the last few years we’ve done a much better job also applying AI to help them with a toolkit, so that they can spend the time on the things that they really care about.” But overall, Wong is bullish on Reddit’s long-term position in the age of AI. “Reddit is basically the taste layer of the internet. No model and no recommendation system can be good, I think, without a dash of Reddit in it, because you just don’t have the freshness of information. That adds value in so many places.” Fortune Daily breaks the traditional barrier between audience and newsroom. The show transforms Fortune ’s trusted reporting into actionable, conversational, and entertaining insights for an emerging class of business leaders. Watch here.

Leadership is aggressively executing high-value data-licensing partnerships with Google and OpenAI, capitalizing on its platform's unique role as the web's authentic conversational repository. However, converting voluntary community contributions into commercial AI training fuel risks alienating the core volunteer moderators who built the platform's proprietary value in the first place.

articles.title: Hyperscale Compute Facilities Transition Into Round-the-Clock Token Foundries
articles.content: SPONSORED FEATURE:  Agentic AI turns inference into a round-the-clock production job. Here's what it takes to keep the tokens flowing in the datacenter you already have. Robin Birtstone Robin Birtstone Published fri 27 Nov 2026 // 01:00 UTC Make us preferred on Google Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. That means they need to think harder about maintenance windows, existing management tooling and predictable deployment. And they'll often be retrofitting halls whose racks rarely draw more than 30 kW. In token factory terms, the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System is the core compute engine. Each system puts eight NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPUs on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, linked by sixth-generation NVLink. ASUS has designed its equipment to support the constraints above. Its customers can choose between the hybrid and fully liquid-cooled models, and they can opt for partial or full rack configurations by buying multiple trays. This enables them to match their facilities' needs. Peak performance versus sustained performance The other difference between model providers and enterprises lies in which numbers they care about. Peak performance is different from sustained performance. The first is a specification sheet number, while the second is what the GPU actually delivers hours into a heavy workload. Production inference tends to run continuously, especially when it uses agents, as opposed to training, which is a sporadic job. So the sustained figure is the one that buyers pay for. Heat becomes a real issue here because when cooling can't keep up, GPUs throttle their clocks to protect themselves. In a token factory, a throttled GPU is a slower production line. The more advanced the architecture becomes, the higher the stakes get. NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPU has raised them to their highest point, delivering up to 400 petaflops of NVFP4 inference per eight-GPU board, according to NVIDIA's sparse specification. This is screamingly fast, but the increased heat per board means less margin before throttling. ASUS designed both models to put direct-to-chip liquid cooling on every GPU. Only the 3U unit leaves the CPUs on air cooling. ASUS also says it puts every configuration through a 168-hour stress test. Power and heat set the shape of the rack As boards increase their compute density, pushing up the power and heat requirements, planning naturally has to move out of the server room and into the facility. That's the case whether you're talking about an entire NVL72 rack or a stack of eight-GPU servers like the ASUS systems. There are other things to consider beyond heat. Few datacenters run racks drawing more than 30 kilowatts, says th e Uptime Institute . Yet a single liquid-cooled tray of the ASUS systems draws up to 23.9 kilowatts, and a full rack of nine has a power budget of about 216 kilowatts. Floor loading and power distribution matter as much as cooling. NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPU raises the stakes again. The eight-GPU format enables organizations to buy their computing power in more granular steps. That's where the two ASUS systems come into their own. With few enterprises needing a training cluster at NVL72 scale, the advantage is that an HGX box lets them buy AI compute in digestible pieces. The ASUS systems also come with a 54V busbar and cable-free board-to-board design. ASUS says this simplifies assembly and improves reliability. Connectivity, storage and management So that's space, power and heat. But a GPU board won't produce many tokens if the network, storage or operational tooling can't feed it properly. Agent workloads move context and data all the time, so east-west bandwidth and local storage are key to effective utilization. Any new equipment should ideally slot straight into the enterprise's existing management and monitoring tooling. ASUS ships the whole rack, including servers, networking, power and storage, as a single blueprint. ASUS pre-validates this AI Factory reference architecture at rack scale so that organizations can plan for future growth. That includes dedicated management nodes and a management switch. Inside each tray, ASUS has sized the data paths to keep the GPUs fed. Eight OSFP ports on NVIDIA ConnectX-9 give every GPU 800Gb/s of east-west bandwidth to the rest of the cluster, and an NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPU adds two 400GbE ports. Within the board, the eight GPUs talk to each other over NVLink at 3,600GB/s, ASUS says. The 2U tray takes up to 4TB of DDR5 system memory and has eight E1.S NVMe bays for fast local data access, while the 3U model offers a choice of U.2 or E1.S drives. Built to be serviced The other issue for enterprises putting AI inference into production is service and maintenance. In a liquid-cooled box, routine fixes can mean draining a coolant loop, which is downtime, and lost token output, that most enterprises can't afford, especially when dealing with non-batch workloads such as inferencing. So ASUS set out to make components quicker to swap. On the 2U fully liquid-cooled model, ASUS did it with independent, tool-less CPU and GPU sleds, each with its own direct-to-chip cooling. On the 3U hybrid, ASUS says the air-cooled CPU sled cuts maintenance time by up to 50 percent. From loading dock to first token Services aren't just about server maintenance. They're also about decreasing the time to value for AI. Most enterprises won't have in-house rack-scale GPU integration skills, which is why pre-validation and design services are so important. ASUS says its services run from early facility assessment through to operations. Its professional services co ver five offerings: infrastructure design, deployment, performance optimization, AI platform development and lifecycle management. For rapid deployment, ASUS uses its own automation platform, the ASUS Infrastructure Deployment Center (AIDC). Production needs a partner, not just a part number So, with an enterprise token factory judged on how reliably it keeps producing rather than on peak FLOPS, in-house AI deployment teams will be back to focusing on the basics, albeit while dealing with an innovative technology. That means they'll be asking questions about sustained performance, heat and power in existing facilities. They'll be looking at integration at the rack level and with management software, along with service windows and deployment time. ASUS is positioning itself as a partner that can answer those questions with the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System, which it's making available this quarter. articles.title: Latin American Mineral Riches Face AI Data Center Infrastructure Bottlenecks
articles.content: LivestreamMenuRising data center and electrification demand is increasing the value of Latin America’s copper, energy and mineral resources.Chile, Argentina and Brazil show different parts of the investment case, from copper supply and refining to export infrastructure, renewable power and rare-earth production.For investors, the key question is whether infrastructure, financing conditions and policy stability can turn those resources into viable projects.Latin America’s copper, energy and mineral resources could play a growing role in supplying the global artificial-intelligence build-out, as data centers and electrification drive demand for power and raw materials. But for investors, it's less about whether Latin America has the resources than whether governments can turn them into viable projects. "We are going through an acceleration in energy demand growth. We need every possible energy source available," Michele Della Vigna, head of natural resources research for Goldman Sachs, told CNBC. "Ultimately, what drives economic growth is energy," he added. Ben Kumar, head of strategy for wealth, investment and public policy at 7IM, suggested Latin America could benefit, given the physical materials needed for AI equipment and data centers. "We are currently neutral in the short term, but if the materials and mining cycle continues, we could see this moving to positive in a few months," he said. The investment case varies across the region. Chile has copper; Argentina is expanding oil and gas exports; and Brazil has abundant renewable power and significant rare earth reserves. Chile's copper sector illustrates both the supply potential and the constraints to expanding supply. Copper production fell 8.5% in the first nine months of 2026, according to the state copper commission Cochilco, as lower ore grades, maintenance, and operational disruptions constrained supply. But demand for refined copper is set to grow 1.6% this year and 2% next year, according to the International Copper Study Group. Supply is struggling to keep pace with demand from expanding electricity grids. Chile's copper commission has raised its 2027 price forecast to $5.95 a pound, from $5.10. Codelco, the state-owned copper producer, may also have scope to increase supply, including through proposed public-private partnerships. Rafael Ch, partner and senior analyst for Latin America and emerging markets at Signum Global Advisors, sees demand continuing to grow. "As countries expand electricity grids, they need more copper regardless of which power source they choose," he said. The scale of the opportunity will depend in part on how quickly energy demand grows. Goldman Sachs forecasts that global power demand for data centers will grow by 170% by 2030. The IEA projected in April that global data center electricity consumption would rise from 485 terawatt-hours in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030. The investment case also depends on whether the region can capture more value from the resources it produces. Latin America and the Caribbean refined only 26% of the copper they mined in 2025, according to the IEA. "Cautious optimism is justified and there will be massive critical mineral demand," said Monica de Bolle, senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics. "But improving refining capacity will be crucial to capture more of that value," she added. Some projects have already secured financing. Chilean explorer Marimaca Copper Corp selected a preferred lender for a $400 million debt facility to build a mine on Oct. 28. The funding will go towards developing an open-pit mine in the north of Chile that will produce 50,000 metric tons of refined copper annually. Production is expected from 2029. Argentina shows the other side of the opportunity: strong oil and gas resources, but insufficient infrastructure to get more production to global markets. "I see an opportunity in the infrastructure that gets Argentine oil and gas to market. A producer in Vaca Muerta can have excellent wells and still struggle to expand exports without pipeline capacity and access to ports. That gives investors a reason to look at transport and export infrastructure alongside production," Rafael Ch, partner and senior analyst for Latin America and emerging markets at Signum Global Advisors, added. Vaca Muerta is Argentina's vast shale basin. Argentina is also attracting investment in drilling and export infrastructure. International capital markets have reopened to investment in drilling and pipelines in Argentina. That investment has already driven the build-out of a pipeline and port. Argentina will then be able to export far more crude oil. Chevron and American oil tycoon Harold Hamm have also increased their investments in Argentina. Brazil's case rests partly on its renewable-heavy power mix. About 89% of the country's electricity was generated from renewable sources in 2025, according to the country's Ministry of Mines and Energy. "That puts Brazil in a strong position to benefit as AI and data centers drive up demand," Stephanie Link, chief investment strategist and portfolio manager at Hightower Advisors, told CNBC. But while Brazil has the world's second-largest reported rare-earth reserves, its estimated mine production is far smaller than China's. USGS estimates put Brazil's output at 2,000 metric tons in 2025, compared with China's 270,000 metric tons. Brazil's reserves are estimated at 11 million metric tons by the USGS, second only to China's 44 million metric tons. For investors, the gap between Brazil's vast reserves and limited current production is both the opportunity and the execution risk. For investors, the policy question is whether governments can make projects viable and keep them on track. Luis Costa, Citi's global head of emerging markets strategy, said governments need to offer incentives, particularly in the early stages of projects, because infrastructure lags the region's resource wealth. He also stressed that support must last: infrastructure projects can take several years to develop. The World Bank's Latin America and the Caribbean Economic Update for 2026 projects growth for the region of 2.2%, and highlights the "restricted fiscal space, sticky inflation and high borrowing costs." "The economic policy and fiscal policy needs to get in line as markets are globally becoming more sensitive to fiscal stories," said Costa. Brazil will need to establish fiscal credibility to attract investment, particularly if higher public spending puts additional pressure on debt and borrowing costs. "If investors doubt the government can stabilize public debt, companies' long-term financing costs could stay high even as the central bank lowers its policy rate," Ch added. With Argentina set for national elections in October 2027, political continuity will also matter for energy investment. "A return to tighter currency controls or persistent deficits would make companies more likely to delay projects, even in an oil field with attractive economics," said Ch. Pro-business President Javier Milei faces a tight race for re-election, though a change in leadership would not necessarily undermine medium- to long-term investment. "There is also the possibility of a pragmatic Peronist ticket emerging, which markets would be satisfied with," said Nicolas Jaquier, emerging-market fixed-income portfolio manager at Ninety One. For those governing across Latin America, policies to unlock its wealth of resources will be key for it to emerge as a winner from the AI demand boom. "Supply chain security is becoming more and more relevant, and if commodities take off Latin America can be a clear and obvious winner," said Kumar.

articles.title: Australian Gas Mandate Seizes One-Fifth of Export Volumes for Grids

Photograph: Manfred Gottschalk/Getty Images Coalition teams up with Labor to pass 20% gas reservation scheme for Australia’s largest exporters Labor passes final major piece of legislation for 2026, denying Greens’ bid for 25% tax on exports Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast A federal gas reservation scheme requiring Australia’s largest exporters to keep up to 20% of their product for domestic use will go ahead with the Coalition’s support. The opposition waved through the government’s plans in the in a late night Senate sitting on Thursday night, giving Labor the numbers it needed. A short sitting of the lower house rubber stamped changes, seeing the legislation pass parliament. The scheme will begin in January 2028. On Friday, the resources minister, Madeleine King, said it would deliver cheaper gas prices for Australians but could not say by how much. “We don’t want to set a figure at this time because the experience with price caps when you name a figure is that also becomes the floor, the lower price,” she said. “And we want to make sure the market’s able to operate to drive prices down as far as they can.” Speaking in the upper house on Thursday, the shadow resources minister, Susan McDonald, said the Coalition would not oppose the scheme after weeks of hard negotiations between the two major parties. Australia projected to completely miss 2035 emissions target without new climate policies Read more “The Coalition will act in the national interest,” she said. “We will allow the government’s proposal to move forward because we do believe in a domestic gas reservation and more gas being made available to Australia.” Labor granted Western Australia a permanent carve-out after lobbying from the federal Coalition and the state’s premier, Roger Cook. On Friday, King said: “WA is really the inspiration for this national scheme because they’ve had a scheme since 2008, which has been really important for gas prices and supply in WA.” WA has an existing scheme that requires exporters to reserve 15% of liquified natural gas (LNG) for the domestic market over the life of a development. That target has not yet been met. Cook said in August the proportion of LNG delivered to the domestic market was 8.7% in 2021 and rose to 12.5% by 2025 . Business groups and gas companies pressured the federal Coalition to do a deal with Labor to keep the Greens out of negotiations. The industry minister, Tim Ayres, said the changes would deliver “fundamental economic reform that will make Australia stronger”. “Australia’s gas is a national asset, and that national asset should be managed in the national interest,” he said. skip past newsletter promotion after newsletter promotion “This is not an export ban, nor is it an export cap. It is a predictable and proportional contribution to domestic supply.” Ayres said Australia would remain a reliable supplier of gas for its key partners. The key sticking point between the parties was the government’s requirement for gas companies to oversupply the market by 10%, which is designed to drive down prices for households and industry. This will remain in place. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here The Coalition originally argued this would lower prices to a level that would dry up future gas investment. They have secured a statutory review to assess the impact of a reservation policy on investment after five years. The Greens demanded a 25% tax on gas exports in return for their support and voted against the scheme in its current form. The minor party’s leader, David Shoebridge , condemned the scheme as a “stitch-up” against the Australian public. “This week, parliament ends with Labor and the Coalition cutting their deal for the gas industry, delivering for the 1% of their corporate donors,” he said before the vote in the Senate. The lower house is set to sit for a short period on Friday morning, a day later than expected, in order to pass legislation amended in the Senate. articles.title: Takealot Absorbs Heavy Losses to Defend South African Commerce From Temu
articles.content: Free Reads Takealot Is Holding Off Deep-Pocketed Global Rivals, But It’s Proving Costly By Henry Nzekwe  |  November 26, 2026 South Africa’s top online retailer Takealot grew revenue 27% to USD 571 M in the six months to September, parent Naspers reported on Wednesday, as it absorbed the arrival of Amazon’s Prime subscription service and competition from Shein and Temu. Its gross merchandise value climbed 16%, and adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation reached USD 37 M, up 21% in local currency. Those are the numbers Naspers put out this week, though they are also the easy part of the story. The harder part sits in a line Naspers did not lead with. Despite the growth, the board has still not reversed the ZAR 5.9 B (~USD 335 M) impairment it booked against Takealot two years ago; a signal that the parent company, for all the upbeat language about competing and doing well, is not yet ready to declare the war won. Takealot’s position is stronger than the doomsayers predicted when Amazon arrived in May 2024. World Wide Worx puts Takealot at 35.3% of online shoppers, ahead of Shein at 21.5% and Amazon at 12.7% before Prime launched in June. Takealot’s local network is real. More than 59,000 earning opportunities depend on the group, including 25,000 small and medium businesses and 20,000 delivery drivers. That infrastructure is expensive to replicate, and it is the main reason Takealot has not been flattened, observers reckon. TakealotMORE, the paid membership programme built to answer Amazon Prime’s ZAR 59.00 (USD 3.35) monthly offer, grew subscription revenue 66%. But Naspers still will not disclose how many members it has. The growth is also volume-led, driven by order counts and conversion rather than pricing power. Naspers said Takealot absorbed a fuel cost headwind and still broke even at operating level, against a USD 4 M loss a year earlier, though some might point out that breaking even is not the same as winning. Meanwhile, there is an awkward contradiction in the strategy. Takealot has been expanding its cross-border marketplace and onboarding Chinese sellers , the same supply chain that South African regulators are trying to tax to protect local retailers from Shein and Temu. Takealot has itself alleged that Shein and Temu exploit tax loopholes. The company is now borrowing a page from the playbook it criticised. Fabricio Bloisi, chief executive of Naspers and Prosus, told journalists the group is competing and doing well. Frederik Zietsman, Takealot’s group CEO, has said the arrival of Amazon Prime marked the start of the game rather than the end of it. Both statements are defensible, but neither changes the fact that Takealot’s first full-year profit, reported in June, came fifteen years after launch, and that the half-year operating result is still a break-even. Takealot has kept the deep-pocketed rivals at bay for another reporting cycle. The impairment sitting on Naspers’ balance sheet suggests the fight is far from settled.

articles.title: Sydney Runway Airspace Close Call Triggers Cockpit Automation Investigation
articles.content: The ATSB said the Qantas flight from Melbourne was due to land just before 10.15am on Wednesday when it cancelled its descent into Sydney airport. Photograph: Hollie Adams/Reuters View image in fullscreen The ATSB said the Qantas flight from Melbourne was due to land just before 10.15am on Wednesday when it cancelled its descent into Sydney airport. Photograph: Hollie Adams/Reuters Qantas and Air New Zealand planes too close at Sydney airport as ‘mental models’ of crews to be investigated Aborted descent on Wednesday morning is latest in a series of landing incidents at Sydney airport Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The Australian Transport Safety Bureau is investigating flight crews’ “mental models” after a Qantas plane aborted its landing at Sydney airport on Wednesday after noticing another aircraft crossing the runway while on its descent. The ATSB said Qantas flight 426 from Melbourne was due to land just before 10.15am on Wednesday, with the Boeing 737 jet told to expect a late landing clearance due to aircraft crossing the runway. As the Qantas plane continued to approach the airport, and before it received a clearance to land, the crew reported seeing an Air New Zealand plane crossing the runway. The Qantas crew decided to conduct a go-around, aborting the landing before trying again. The ATSB said it would investigate what it called an “aircraft separation issue”. The agency will gather evidence, including interviewing flight crew, looking at flight data and monitoring air traffic control audio and any available CCTV into the incident. “In particular, the investigation will seek to ascertain what information was provided to the crews of both aircraft, and what mental models those crews held,” the agency said in a statement. Concern over Sydney airport as near misses and runway incursions at 20% above national average Read more “The ATSB notes that, during the occurrence, important safety defences were in place and operated, such as the flight crew’s go-around decision.” A preliminary report should be complete in about eight weeks, the ATSB said. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Qantas did not immediately reply to a request for comment. “Our pilots were following air traffic control instructions and elected to conduct a go-around as the other aircraft was crossing the runway,” the airline told the Sydney Morning Herald. Sydney airport has seen a series of near-miss incidents this year, including when a Jetstar plane narrowly avoided a collision with a Qatar Airways plane on the tarmac in August. In another incident, a Virgin plane was forced to abort takeoff when a Qantas plane began to cross the runway in front of it. Angus Mitchell, the ATSB chief commissioner, released preliminary investigation reports in September that found staffing levels at Sydney airport had “emerged as a recurring area of inquiry”, with a review finding runway incursions and near misses at 20% above national averages there. “This should be viewed in the context of Sydney airport being the most complex in the country,” Mitchell said at the time. The ATSB stressed it “has yet to determine whether staff resourcing factors directly contributed to any occurrence, or whether they were simply underlying conditions that were recognised and being effectively managed by Airservices, Australia’s air traffic services provider”. The ATSB added Friday its examination of the recent incident would seek to look at safety defences in place “and to establish or rule out any underlying safety issues and contributing factors common across the other occurrences at Sydney airport currently under investigation”. articles.title: Algorithmic Pricing Surveillance Exploits Low-Income Consumers During Flash Sales
articles.content: 26 de novembro de 2026 04:00 Por Gabriel Teles Faça da Pública sua fonte preferida Nos adicione como fonte preferencial no Google. Não deixe a Publica sumir Nos adicione como fonte preferencial no Google. --> Divulgação Amazon/www.aboutamazon.com.br/ comércio economia Justiça saúde segurança tecnologia trabalho Todos os anos, quando chega a Black Friday, voltam a circular denúncias sobre as estratégias utilizadas pelas empresas para enganar os consumidores. A mais conhecida delas consiste em aumentar artificialmente os preços nas semanas anteriores, para depois anunciar descontos que, na realidade, pouco ou nada representam. É a famosa promoção pela “metade do dobro”. Essas práticas merecem ser denunciadas. Entretanto, existe um aspecto mais profundo da Black Friday que raramente aparece nas discussões públicas: a exploração e a precarização do trabalho daqueles que tornam possível a circulação de milhões de mercadorias em um intervalo tão curto. Por trás das propagandas, dos descontos e das promessas de entrega rápida, existe uma extensa infraestrutura logística sustentada pelo trabalho de milhares de pessoas. São trabalhadores que descarregam caminhões, recebem mercadorias, organizam estoques, separam pedidos, embalam produtos e preparam encomendas para expedição. Sem essas atividades, nenhuma das grandes plataformas de comércio eletrônico conseguiria cumprir aquilo que promete aos consumidores. A dimensão dessa infraestrutura pode ser percebida pelos próprios números do setor. Segundo projeções da Associação Brasileira de Inteligência Artificial e E-commerce (Abiacom), a semana da Black Friday de 2026 deverá movimentar aproximadamente R$ 16,6 bilhões no comércio eletrônico brasileiro, crescimento de 24,4% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. A quantidade de pedidos deverá passar de 16,51 milhões para 21,66 milhões, um aumento de 31,2% em apenas um ano. Essas milhões de mercadorias precisam ser movimentadas em um período curto. Cada pedido realizado pelo consumidor corresponde a uma sequência de operações, desde a localização do produto no estoque até sua expedição e entrega. Uma das principais respostas empresariais consiste na contratação massiva de trabalhadores temporários. Somente neste mês de novembro de 2026 a Amazon anunciou a abertura de 12 mil vagas temporárias para atender ao aumento da demanda durante a Black Friday. A empresa informou também que sua infraestrutura logística brasileira havia alcançado 350 unidades, após a abertura de mais de 120 instalações desde a Black Friday anterior. A DHL Supply Chain, uma das maiores empresas de logística do mundo, anunciou a previsão de contratar aproximadamente 2,6 mil trabalhadores temporários adicionais durante a temporada de Black Friday e Natal. Esse contingente representa um aumento de 38% nas contratações temporárias em relação a um mês convencional. A empresa projeta movimentar mais de 37 milhões de unidades no comércio eletrônico durante o período, volume 19% superior ao de um mês convencional. A Americanas, por sua vez, anunciou mais de 3,7 mil vagas temporárias, das quais aproximadamente 760 seriam destinadas às operações logísticas. Os anúncios empresariais apresentam essas contratações como oportunidades de emprego e demonstrações do dinamismo econômico do setor. Entretanto, grande parte desse contingente de temporários trabalha sob rotinas exaustivas, com funções repetitivas e metas rígidas, altamente vigiados por sistemas tecnológicos, além de não terem segurança do que vai acontecer quando o período de vendas passa.  A legislação brasileira reconhece o trabalho temporário como modalidade destinada a atender necessidades transitórias de substituição de pessoal ou demandas complementares de serviços. Quando a demanda diminui, as empresas podem reduzir o contingente sem necessariamente incorporar aqueles que foram mobilizados para sustentar a expansão das vendas. Centro de Distribuição da Amazon em Recife, inaugurado em 2024 Em abril de 2025, publiquei no Le Monde Diplomatique o artigo Galpões logísticos e os novos rostos da exploração , no qual discutia como a expansão do comércio eletrônico estava acompanhada pela constituição de novos espaços de exploração do trabalho. Naquele momento, chamei atenção para uma contradição: as grandes plataformas anunciavam uma economia cada vez mais automatizada, enquanto seus centros de distribuição continuavam dependendo de uma imensa quantidade de trabalho humano, submetido a formas sofisticadas de controle da produtividade. Desde então, minha pesquisa em sociologia do trabalho permitiu avançar na investigação desse processo. Durante uma experiência de campo realizada em 2026, acompanhei diretamente o cotidiano de trabalho no interior de um centro de distribuição. A observação das atividades permitiu compreender aspectos que dificilmente aparecem nas descrições institucionais sobre eficiência logística e modernização tecnológica. No setor de recebimento, por exemplo, as mercadorias chegavam organizadas em grandes volumes e precisavam ser descarregadas, abertas, identificadas e encaminhadas para as etapas seguintes. Os trabalhadores utilizavam coletores eletrônicos para registrar produtos e alimentar os sistemas digitais responsáveis pela organização do fluxo de mercadorias. Cada operação precisava ser executada de acordo com procedimentos definidos. A leitura de códigos de barras, a identificação dos produtos e sua movimentação entre diferentes áreas produziam informações incorporadas continuamente aos sistemas de gestão do armazém. A presença da tecnologia era constante. Entretanto, o funcionamento desses sistemas dependia de uma atividade física intensa. Jornadas de doze horas, longos períodos em pé, movimentos repetitivos e cansaço acumulado ao final dos turnos compunham o cotidiano observado. A execução das atividades também exigia conhecimentos práticos que ultrapassavam as prescrições dos sistemas digitais. Trabalhadores precisavam compreender o funcionamento dos equipamentos, resolver situações imprevistas e aprender procedimentos que frequentemente dependiam da experiência de outros colegas. Os softwares de gestão, os dispositivos de leitura e os sistemas automatizados ampliam a capacidade de acompanhar a movimentação das mercadorias. Simultaneamente, permitem registrar informações sobre a execução das atividades, identificar interrupções e produzir indicadores utilizados pela gestão empresarial. A digitalização também reorganiza a relação entre concepção e execução das tarefas. Parte do conhecimento necessário à coordenação do processo de trabalho é incorporada aos sistemas digitais, enquanto os trabalhadores passam a executar atividades cuja sequência é definida por esses dispositivos. O conceito de taylorismo digital ajuda a compreender essa configuração, especialmente quando os mecanismos de controle digital são associados à fragmentação das atividades e à imposição de metas de produtividade. Diferentes mecanismos são utilizados nos centros de distribuição para aumentar a intensidade do trabalho. Entre eles estão a imposição de metas, a vigilância digital, a fragmentação das tarefas e a reorganização dos tempos de trabalho. Uma inovação tecnológica pode reduzir deslocamentos, eliminar determinadas tarefas e diminuir o esforço exigido dos trabalhadores. Mas em outras situações, os ganhos operacionais são acompanhados pela ampliação das metas e pelo aumento da quantidade de atividades exigidas durante a jornada. É nessa relação que a discussão sobre eficiência logística encontra a questão da exploração do trabalho. Trabalhadores de centros galpões de distribuição passam por jornadas de doze horas, com longos períodos de pé e fazendo movimentos repetitivos Em setembro de 2026, publiquei, em coautoria com Livia de Tommasi, o artigo A nova geografia do varejo brasileiro , também no Le Monde Diplomatique Brasil . Naquele texto, analisamos como a expansão do comércio eletrônico participa de uma reorganização das infraestruturas comerciais brasileiras. Parte das atividades anteriormente concentradas nas lojas físicas é deslocada para centros de distribuição, instalações de armazenagem e redes logísticas que passam a ocupar uma posição estratégica na circulação das mercadorias. A concorrência entre as plataformas envolve a capacidade de oferecer mercadorias a preços competitivos, mantendo uma infraestrutura capaz de assegurar entregas rápidas e previsíveis. Para isso, as empresas precisam reduzir os intervalos entre o recebimento dos pedidos, sua preparação e a distribuição das mercadorias. A circulação das mercadorias precisa ser cada vez mais rápida, mais ágil. Entretanto, o tempo economizado na circulação precisa ser produzido — e aí entram os trabalhadores, que entram e saem desse circuito conforme os interesses das empresas. Na tela do aplicativo, a compra pode ser concluída em poucos segundos. O consumidor acompanha a confirmação do pagamento, a preparação da encomenda, sua expedição e o deslocamento até o endereço de entrega. Toda a operação aparece como resultado de um sistema tecnológico integrado. Dentro do centro de distribuição, cada atualização corresponde a processos realizados por trabalhadores. A mesma infraestrutura que permite oferecer entregas cada vez mais rápidas concentra trabalhadores submetidos a processos de trabalho intensamente precarizados e monitorados. A ampliação das capacidades tecnológicas não elimina as relações de exploração que sustentam o funcionamento dessas empresas. Na Black Friday, a contradição adquire uma expressão particularmente evidente. Milhões de consumidores são mobilizados por campanhas publicitárias que celebram descontos e oportunidades de compra. Simultaneamente, milhares de trabalhadores são incorporados temporariamente às operações logísticas para assegurar o processamento das mercadorias. Passado o período, para as empresas, ficam os números de faturamento, pedidos e participação de mercado. Para parte dos trabalhadores temporários, pode significar também o encerramento do contrato de trabalho e o retorno à procura por emprego. Essas condições de trabalho já ultrapassaram o terreno das denúncias individuais e passaram a ser objeto de investigações, autuações e decisões da Justiça do Trabalho. Em setembro de 2026, por exemplo, o Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) obteve uma decisão judicial determinando alterações nas jornadas e nas condições de descanso dos trabalhadores do centro logístico da Amazon em Santa Maria, no Distrito Federal. A investigação identificou jornadas de 11 e 12 horas, atividades realizadas predominantemente em pé e irregularidades relacionadas aos intervalos de descanso. A decisão determinou a concessão de pausas de dez minutos a cada 90 minutos de trabalho em pé, a disponibilização de assentos e a adequação das escalas aos limites legais, ressalvadas as hipóteses autorizadas pela legislação. Outro dado desse mesmo caso é particularmente revelador. Segundo informações da fiscalização realizada em março de 2026, havia 1.398 trabalhadores no complexo logístico: 485 contratados diretamente pela Ceva Logistics, responsável pela operação, e outros 913 vinculados a empresas de trabalho temporário. Isso significa que aproximadamente 65% dos trabalhadores identificados naquela fiscalização estavam contratados por meio dessa modalidade. Em outubro de 2025, outra decisão judicial, também obtida pelo MPT, determinou que a empresa responsável pela operação de um galpão do Mercado Livre em Presidente Prudente (SP) adotasse medidas de proteção à saúde e à segurança dos trabalhadores. A fiscalização havia identificado irregularidades ergonômicas, ausência de avaliação adequada dos riscos ocupacionais e problemas relacionados ao trabalho realizado em pé e à movimentação de cargas. A operação processava aproximadamente 12 mil mercadorias por dia. Um caso ainda mais expressivo ocorreu em São José do Rio Preto (SP). Em novembro de 2026, a Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho concluiu uma investigação em centros de distribuição vinculados a uma plataforma de marketplace. Foram identificados 796 trabalhadores sem registro em carteira, muitos deles recrutados por meio de uma cadeia de empresas terceirizadas e remunerados por diária. A fiscalização resultou em 51 autos de infração contra oito empresas, totalizando R$ 7,97 milhões em multas administrativas. As irregularidades ultrapassavam a questão contratual. Os auditores identificaram riscos de atropelamento por caminhões, choques elétricos e incêndios. Um dos galpões chegou a ser interditado em maio de 2026, diante do risco grave e iminente à segurança dos trabalhadores. Mesmo após a interdição, a fiscalização encontrou pessoas trabalhando no local, utilizando a iluminação dos próprios celulares. A unidade somente foi liberada no final de julho, depois da realização de adequações. Esses episódios não ocorreram necessariamente durante a Black Friday, tampouco permitem afirmar que todos os centros de distribuição funcionem nas mesmas condições. Entretanto, mostram problemas que atravessam a organização do trabalho logístico e ajudam a compreender as condições dos períodos de maior demanda. As mesmas empresas e operações que apresentam a eficiência logística como expressão do desenvolvimento tecnológico precisam responder judicialmente por questões elementares relacionadas às jornadas, aos intervalos de descanso, à ergonomia e à segurança dos trabalhadores. A multiplicação de empresas intermediárias pode dificultar a identificação das responsabilidades trabalhistas, enquanto a empresa que controla a infraestrutura e organiza a circulação das mercadorias preserva sua capacidade de comandar o processo logístico. Por isso, a discussão sobre a Black Friday precisa ultrapassar a denúncia das manipulações de preços. Afinal, enquanto as empresas divulgam o preço das mercadorias e o tempo necessário para entregá-las, as jornadas, as condições de segurança, o desgaste físico e a insegurança dos trabalhadores temporários não encontram espaço nas mesmas propagandas. É esse o verdadeiro lado oculto da Black Friday. articles.title: Decentralized Smart Surveillance Networks Accelerate Privatized Neighborhood Defense
articles.content: Founded in 2024 by Nick Mills and Michael Houghton, Community Wolf started with a WhatsApp number that lets anyone report crime and suspicious activity for free, anonymously and in their first language. Its AI models structure the images, video and pin drops users submit, then alert people nearby and local responders. The startup – recently a winner at the South African Startup Awards – has since added emergency assistance, family safety, community communication and operational software for security operators. It has more than 700,000 users and has recorded over 180,000 incidents. Terra Industries, also founded in 2024, builds autonomous security systems to protect critical infrastructure such as mines, power plants and pipelines across Africa and the Global South. Its air, land and maritime systems run on ArtemisOS, its software platform for large-scale security operations. Disrupt Africa reported in August the company had raised an additional US$18 million in strategic funding to close its own seed round at US$52 million. The investment in CommunityWolf, the amount of which is undisclosed, marks Terra’s entry into public safety, with Terra CEO Nathan Nwachuku joining Community Wolf’s board. Community Wolf will use the funding to expand into communities around critical and urban infrastructure, while the two companies will also look at linking Community Wolf’s products to Terra’s software, so verified incidents reach Terra’s command centres alongside drone and sensor data. “The people living around critical assets like mines are the first to feel an attack, and they are often the first to see it coming,” said Nwachuku. “We believe communal security will also be pivotal in how we protect lives and secure infrastructure.” “Community Wolf gives residents a way to report and security operators an integrated platform to manage their communication and response,” said Mills. “Alongside Terra’s autonomous ground and aerial systems, we can keep millions more people safe across the continent.” Passionate about the vibrant tech startups scene in Africa, Tom can usually be found sniffing out the continent's most exciting new companies and entrepreneurs, funding rounds and any other developments within the growing ecosystem. The rapid growth of private sensor grids highlights the structural retreat of public policing across developing states in favor of hyper-securitized, subscription-funded civilian surveillance.
